examples.title: Stopping a Change
examples.code:
<SegmentedControl aria-label="Visibility" defaultValue="private">
  <SegmentedControl.Segment value="private">Private</SegmentedControl.Segment>
  <SegmentedControl.Segment
    value="public"
    onClick={event => {
      if (!window.confirm('Anyone with the link will see it.')) {
        event.preventDefault();
      }
    }}
  >
    Public
  </SegmentedControl.Segment>
</SegmentedControl>

examples.title: Compound (dot-notation) usage

accessibility:
`SegmentedControl` follows the
[APG radio group pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/), which is what the
[APG toolbar example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/examples/toolbar/) uses for
its alignment buttons: "since pressing one toggles off another so that only one button in the group
is in the pressed state, the toggles behave like radio buttons."

- **Roles and state:** the row is `role="radiogroup"`, and each segment is a native
  `<button type="button">` with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked` set to `"true"` or `"false"` from
  the first render, server markup included. There's no `aria-pressed`: a segment is checked or not,
  not pressed.
- **A name for the group:** a radio group needs one, so pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. A
  development build warns when it has neither.
- **One tab stop:** the checked segment holds it, or the first enabled segment while none is
  checked. While focus is in the row the stop goes with it, so Tab always leaves from where you
  are.
- **The check follows focus:** the arrow keys, Home and End check the segment they move to, as
  native radio buttons do. A screen reader announces the new segment as checked straight away.
- **It can't be cleared:** once a segment is checked, one always is. Pressing the checked segment
  again keeps it checked and doesn't call `onChange`.
- **Icon-only segments** need an `aria-label`, as on `Button`.
- **Checked is easy to see:** the default `link` fill turns a light segment solid blue, and a dark
  one bright in dark mode, so it's a change in lightness and not only in hue. `color` leaves out the
  fills that wouldn't be, the same way `ToggleButton` does.
- **Not a form field:** it's always `type="button"`, so it never submits a form, and it carries no
  value. A choice the form should send is `Radios`.
summary: The `SegmentedControl` component renders a row of buttons where only one can be on, and tells a screen reader it's a radio group. It's Bulma's `.buttons.has-addons` row, with the checked segment filled and marked `is-selected`, the way Bulma's button docs show it. To a screen reader it's `role="radiogroup"`, with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked` on each segment, which is how the APG toolbar example marks its alignment buttons. The keys follow the APG radio group: the row is one tab stop, the arrow keys move to the next or previous enabled segment and check it, wrapping at either end, Home and End go to the first and last, and Space checks the focused segment. Once a segment is checked, one always is. It carries no form value. A choice that's sent with a form is `Radios`.

props.name: value
props.description: The checked segment's `value`, when you hold the state. Setting it makes the group controlled: picking a segment only calls `onChange`, and nothing changes until you pass the new value. `null` checks nothing. Pick this or `defaultValue` for the group's lifetime.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The segment checked to begin with, when the group holds its own state. Leave it out and nothing is checked until someone picks one, and Tab lands on the first enabled segment meanwhile.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the newly checked segment's `value`, whether or not `value` is set. The arrow keys, Home and End check the segment they move to, so each of those calls it too: the check follows focus, as in a native radio group. Pressing the checked segment again doesn't call it, since a segmented control can't be cleared: one stays checked once one is.

props.name: color
props.description: The checked segment's fill. The others are plain buttons, so the fill is the difference people see. Takes the same colors as `ToggleButton`, for the same reason: `white`, `light`, `dark` and `black` fill about as light or dark as a plain button already is in one theme or the other.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of every segment, through Bulma's `are-<size>` on the row.

props.name: hasAddons
props.description: Joins the segments into one row with no gap between them, Bulma's `has-addons`. Set it to `false` for separate buttons.

props.name: isRight
props.description: Aligns the row to the right.

props.name: children
props.description: The `SegmentedControl.Segment`s, each with a `value` of its own.

extraProps.name: aria-label
extraProps.description: Names the group for a screen reader, such as "Text alignment". A radio group needs a name, so pass this or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

extraProps.name: aria-labelledby
extraProps.description: The id of a visible heading or label that names the group, in place of `aria-label`.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One option in the row: a `<button role="radio">` that's checked while the group's value is its `value`, filled with the group's `color` and marked `is-selected`.

props.name: value
props.description: **Required.** What `onChange` reports when this segment is checked, and what the group's `value` and `defaultValue` name it by. Unique within the group.

props.name: children
props.description: The label. An icon on its own needs an `aria-label`, so a screen reader has something to say.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the segment, the same as `disabled`: it can't be clicked, the arrow keys, Home and End skip it, and it never holds the row's tab stop. A checked one keeps its fill under Bulma's disabled look.
